messages:
ana: FYI customer ACME reported rerank API returning scores that don't map to per-query candidate lists. They sent a batch with multiple queries of varying candidate lengths and the scores look interleaved instead of grouped by query. Posting their original payload (sanitized) and logs below. Can eng take a look?

ana: customer payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-v1",
  "queries": [
    {"query": "find red shoes", "candidates": ["c1", "c2", "c3"]},
    {"query": "blue hat", "candidates": ["d1"]},
    {"query": "green scarf", "candidates": ["e1", "e2"]}
  ],
  "options": {"batch_mode": "multiquery"}
}
```

ana: returned body (redacted):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.7, 0.2, 0.9, 0.85, 0.45, 0.6],
  "meta": {"request_id": "req_abc123456def"}
}
```

ana: The customer expects grouping like [scores for query1 (3 items)], [query2 (1 item)], [query3 (2 items)] but the scores above don't align (order looks interleaved). They tried both SDK and raw curl. No HTTP error codes returned.

mike: Can you paste the exact curl (with auth headers redacted) and the request_id? Also which model version and rerank config (any per_query flags)?

ana: here's the curl they ran (auth redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '@payload.json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: req_abc123456def'
```

ana: they used model `rerank-v1` (no explicit per_query flag in their app). Logs show a match_id entry: `rerank.batch: serialized_candidates_count=6, per_query_mode=false`

kumar: thanks. Suspect serialization codepath that flattens candidates then maps scores using a running global index. If per-query offsets aren't applied correctly when candidate sublists vary, you can end up with interleaving. Did the payload include any empty candidate arrays or nulls?

ana: no empty lists in customer's payload. i made a reduced repro to try to reproduce locally, posted below.

ana: reduced repro payload:
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-v1",
  "queries": [
    {"query": "A", "candidates": ["a1", "a2", "a3"]},
    {"query": "B", "candidates": ["b1"]},
    {"query": "C", "candidates": ["c1", "c2"]}
  ]
}
```

mike: repro'd locally with that payload against `rerank-v1@2026-02-15`. Response I see: 
```json
{
  "scores": [0.12, 0.34, 0.56, 0.78, 0.90, 0.11],
  "meta": {"request_id": "req_local_9f3"}
}
```

mike: expected grouping ([3],[1],[2]) but actual mapping we saw when we attached candidate ids from input to scores: [a1->0.12, b1->0.34, a2->0.56, a3->0.78, c1->0.90, c2->0.11] — clearly wrong ordering.

mike: digging into logs I see: `serialize_candidates() // appended candidate flat list`, then later `map_scores_to_candidates() // using global_index++` but the global_index is not reset per query when candidate_count variable is present. I'm going to assign to runtime.

kumar: got it, reproducible. I pushed a quick patch in a branch that fixes the per-query offset calculation (using per_query_offset variable). Local unit tests added. Planning hotfix to staging first. Temporary workaround for customers: set header `X-Rerank-Candidate-Mapping: per_query` or include explicit `candidate_offsets` array matching queries. We'll document this.

kumar: timeline: hotfix to staging in ~30m, canary to prod in 2h after smoke tests. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging/rerank-fix-2026-03-17 by kumar. ETA 28m.

ana: thanks team. i'll relay workaround to ACME and ask if they'd like us to run an instrumented test with their real request_id. will follow up when staging is live. :thumbsup:
